Do you want powers beyond your wildest imaginations?
Yes, I do!
Are you willing to pay the price?
....

It was under a bridge, with a cool breeze touching my skin. My tears dried up making my cheeks feel sticky. I had a fight with my mom. More like she slapped me when I least expected it. It really hurt you know. The abstract slap that was hit at my intentions. 
I know mothers love their kids, and they sometimes strike as a form of care. As a reflex action that is the result of their worries. I understand that she hit me because she was worried about my rash actions. What I do not understand is, if I, being a kid, far from what a mother is, am able to understand that and think rationally, why are the people including my mother unable to do so. Why do they not understand that my rash actions, my wishes, they concede with my wishes and dreams. Why do they not accept me and love for me, for trying to be a good boy, for doing good things for others, Why did she not hug me, when she knew, that all I wanted was to be a 
                                                                        HERO.

The dream to be a hero often starts when kids see them display strength and put themselves on the line. They either see that in anime, cartoons, TV programs, movies, books, and even stories they might hear from their adults. 
I too was a boy, just like that. Inspired by the feats and strengths of the heroes in anime and books. I too wanted to be loved like them. 

They say when people grow up they experience changes. Apart from the physical changes, the set of values and the personality makes most of what causes these changes. Dreams too play a vital part here. Hence when a person grows up, it is safe to say their dreams grow up too and hence experience changes.
Growing up, I learned the concept of the strong and the weak. I learned about fiction and the practicality of real life. But here, unlike the other kids, with whom I share a reason to be inspired by heroes, I was different. My weakness strengthened my dreams. 
I understood one fundamental pillar of what a hero stands for. Strength is not fundamental to being a hero. Heroes like Mumen Rider are prime examples. Yet being loved by people is also not a necessity as many heroes work from under the spotlight. Yet they all stayed true to one concept. Being a support for the weak. Nothing special or out of the ordinary, just plain old support. 

If a hero is a support for the weak, there must be a set standard for what the weak connotes too. In a world where super strength is an ability, a world-class weightlifter might be weak and unable to do anything, but the world we live in is not that of fiction. Hence why you are weak if you consider yourself weak. A hero is supposed to be the symbol to show them, and especially in this world, it would be even more effective, to show them that they started in the same place yet one is now the pillar for the other. In the wake of all these feelings, I Sanzo Taisuke son of late Sanzo Hattori will never consider myself weak and will aspire to be a real-life hero in my own way. 

I often look at myself in the mirror. My short height of 165cm. Slightly above average build due to the fact that I work out daily, I hope of staying fit and active and ready for action. My shaggy hair and small thin eyes along with my other features do no make me look out to be the hero I hope to be. But I would never let that get to me. There are blessed people, the moment I get hung up on the idea that I am average will become my own grave. As a potential hero, my foremost enemy is my own negativity and my first battle has always been my active cognition not to lose sight of my goal. 

The reason I keep on repeating these thoughts and feelings to me daily is to strengthen my resolve and know what I stand for. Today is the first day at school for me as a second year. I go to a local school near my area. It is a good school. I took my bag and came downstairs. My loving mother had prepared a toast and a glass of milk as always. She too was feeding my 3-year-old kid brother. We had a usual talk. Mainly focussing on how today was my first day as a second-year student in high school. It was the month of April and I had turned 16 last month. Doing my breakfast, I took to my way.

On the way, I saw many kids all going to the same destination as me if not similar. Many of them were in groups or pairs to which I slightly chuckled how I had overlooked such an important thing in my life as to intermingle and make good friends. I had friends, but I had failed to make work on the bond to strengthen it. I was not anti-social either. I was a fairly good participant of the class with my own self being as my cover to define who I was. If someone was to say to choose between the silent and cool versus the passionate and loud, most would probably consider me the first but I actually think I am the latter one. But it is weird how I am unable to channel those feelings out in school in the setting of the classroom. 

I had already asked away where my new class was so I headed straight to the room in the familiar building of the school. I opened the door where a couple of students were already there, Jougasaki Yosuke, the bald fun guy of the class was standing in front of the board were upon my sight he in his loud voice almost screamed, "ENTERRRRR THEEEEEE HEROOOOO" "People, the hero is finally upon us, we are saved, no amount of trouble is a problem anymore, be it the potential chances of Mr. Satou sensei being our homeroom teacher or be it the strict studies, the hero will save the day." "Hero same, please come in and grace us your presence." 
I entered the room chuckling and as expected everyone was laughing. A good start to the day. Yosuke was not particularly close with me but he was like that with everyone. He was in the same class as me last year too. The other faces were also recognizable so our class was mostly the same. Yosuke's words were not out of spite, they were just a superficial label that did not mean much to them. 
It goes back to the first year when a transfer student who was very shy and introverted was being treated harshly by a bunch of girls from another class for god knows what reason in the hallway. I stepped in and without doing much because nothing much was needed, I took her away. She thought it was a petty heroic thing to do and long story short, we got close. And as such, I used to share my feelings with her as she did with me. We were on the way to become good friends but suddenly she had to move away. 
On her last day in class, in a sort of farewell speech, she really mustered up the spirit and thanked everyone for most people in our class were good fellows. In the end, she looked at me and as loud as she could, said out, "Sanzo kun, I believe you can be a hero!!" And embarrassed ran out. I later did meet her again out of school where I thanked her for her support and bid the byes in a good ending route to this romance story that could have taken place.... jokes aside, now you might understand, how the name hero came upon me as a label. ever since then, whenever the need arises to be made fun of, I was referred to as a hero. No one knew the actual reason, as to that it is my real dream and when someone would ask, I would merely shrug it off as a casual thing.

***
I think this is a very relatable thing, when people are free, they think. About things that could have been, or things that should happen in the future revolving all around them. One is the center of thought of one's own self. My wish to be a hero may sound superficial to most and is the reason I do not share it much. I can share the words that can explain logic, but I lack the words to explain the ambition behind it. from one conservative school of thought, maybe I am weak and sefish and to cover that I aspire the image of a hero. But I genuinely am trying to be one. I mean, is it wrong to do so? why is it considered childish, why is the me who was allowed to have the dream to be a hero when I was 8 am not allowed to have one 8 years later. It is not that I want people's affirmation, but support is essential, I cannot deny that. In the previous years, in the so called deciation of being a hero I have often jumped in problems a little hard for little me to handle alone which caused me to suffer physical pain which resulted into the emotional pain for my family. 
After all, I am a human who is in the process of growing up and inconsistency will always be there.

Thinking along these lines, I was made to think of all those people who support the heroes and are their cause and motivation to do better. Caped heroes might have it more easy than us in normal school uniforms. But I do also admit that people gather to you mostly when you give them a reason to. But is being there or being one's self not a reason? My mind was wondering off the idea of a love interest. No matter how beautifully i tried to phrase it. During the lunch break, I had lowered my head and went into the thinking process only as a defence mechanism to avoid the rush of my feelings that I once again feel upon entering the classroom in the morning.

Yoru Sumiko, she is a really pretty girl in my class, just like last year, and I have always harboured a one sided crush and feelings towards her. But due to my nervousness and weird temperament i feel a little reluctant to approach her. Such has caused my time to go on. Surely my adolescent hormones were racing wild and free.

During this thought process, I was touched on my back. I lifted my head to see that it was Ono Nina. She was referred to as Nino by most of the class as a nickname. Nino was a short haired cute girl that was kind and funny and used to communicate good with almost everyone.She was the one I used to talk the most to given the fact that we were in the same class from middle school onwards. But I never really felt a proper friendship between us. There were times I would literally feel as if Nino liked me but my bubble would pop up when I would see her interacting with other people. And if she looked after me to some extent, it must be because of the time she knew me by and her good nature. "Would you like to have lunch with us?" She pointed to a group by the window at the front left side of the room. We were in the right most last lane in the middle. I saw 3 girls and 1 boy sitting there. I thought for a moment but humbly declined. I simply just wasn't in the mood. She smiled and went away, "Please do ask away the next time, I surely will take you up on the offer." I said while she was going away to which she raised as thumbs up.

The day went by without any particular thing, by after noon, I was on my way back to home. The story of my life as a HERO was already in move for a long time, but the time it take a drastic turn was just about near.
